Rashi on Eruvin 82a:10:1.hebrew: כיצד משתתפין כו' וכל מי שמקבל מבעוד יום - לסמוך על עירוב זה ולילך, מותר:
Rashi on Eruvin 82a:10:1.english: How does one participate, etc., and anyone who accepts while it is still day - To rely on this eiruv and go — [he] is permitted.

Rashi on Eruvin 82a:10:2.hebrew: אין מערבין - לא התירו חכמים לצאת חוץ לתחום ע"י עירוב, אלא לדבר מצוה:
Rashi on Eruvin 82a:10:2.english: One may not establish an eiruv - The Sages did not permit going out beyond the [Shabbat] limit by means of an eiruv, except for the purpose of a mitzvah.

Rashi on Eruvin 82a:14:1.hebrew: הודיעוהו מבעוד יום ולא הודיעוהו קתני - הודיעוהו — אע"פ שלא נתרצה מבעוד יום, ונתרצה משחשיכה — אמרינן: הוברר שקודם זמן קניית עירוב דעתו לכך היה. לא הודיעוהו עד שחשיכה — מאי ברירה איכא? הא לא הוה ידע דאיכא עירוב דנימא דעתיה עליה הואי:
Rashi on Eruvin 82a:14:1.english: “They informed him while it was still day and they did not inform him” is what it teaches - [If] they informed him — even though he did not consent while it was still day, and consented [only] after dark — we say: It has been clarified that prior to the time the eiruv took effect, his mind was directed toward this. [If] they did not inform him until after dark, what clarification is there? Behold, he did not know that there was an eiruv, that we could say his mind was upon it!

Rashi on Eruvin 82a:15:1.hebrew: יוצא בעירוב אמו - עירבה אמו לעצמה ולא זיכתה לו בעירוב, מוליכתו עמה, דכגופה דמי; דמסתמא דעתה עליה, דלא סגי ליה בלאו אמו:
Rashi on Eruvin 82a:15:1.english: May go out by means of his mother’s eiruv - [If] his mother made an eiruv for herself and did not confer possession of [a share in] the eiruv to him, she may take him with her, as he is considered like her [own] body; for presumably she had him in mind, since he cannot manage without his mother.

Rashi on Eruvin 82a:16:1.hebrew: ותנן נמי גבי סוכה - כלומר: וכי תימא בן שש "צריך לאמו" קרי ליה — הא ליכא למימר, דתנן נמי גבי סוכה כי האי גוונא, ופרשינן התם: הי קטן צריך לאמו:
Rashi on Eruvin 82a:16:1.english: And we also learned with regard to sukka - That is to say: And if you should say that [the baraita] calls a six-year-old [one who] "needs his mother" — this cannot be said, for we also learned similarly with regard to sukka, and we explained there which child needs his mother.

Rashi on Eruvin 82a:16:2.english: Is obligated in a sukka - We train him rabbinically.

Rashi on Eruvin 82a:18:1.hebrew: ואינו קורא אימא - כיון דלא קרי ההיא שעתא, לאו צריך הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 82a:18:1.english: And does not call: Mother - Since he does not call at that time, he does not need [his mother].

Rashi on Eruvin 82a:18:2.hebrew: ופרכינן אימא סלקא דעתך גדול נמי קרי - כלומר, לא משוית ליה אין צריך לאמו עד שיהא ניעור משנתו ולא יקרא "אימא"? הא אי קרא "אימא" — צריך לאמו משוית ליה? הא אפילו גדול דרכו בכך:
Rashi on Eruvin 82a:18:2.english: And we object: "Can it enter your mind [that calling] 'Mother' [means he needs her]? An older [child] also calls" - That is to say: Do you not consider him [to be one who] does not need his mother until he awakens from his sleep and does not call "Mother"? But if he called "Mother," you would consider him [to be one who] needs his mother? Yet even an older [child] is accustomed to doing so!

Rashi on Eruvin 82a:18:3.hebrew: אלא כל שניעור משנתו ואינו קורא אימא אימא - דלא צוח עד דאתיא לקמיה, הוי אינו צריך לאמו:
Rashi on Eruvin 82a:18:3.english: Rather, any [child] who wakens from his sleep and does not call “Mother, Mother” - [One] who does not cry out until she comes before him is [considered] one who does not need his mother.

Rashi on Eruvin 82a:19:1.english: And how much - How many years old is he?

Rashi on Eruvin 82a:19:2.hebrew: כבר ארבע כבר חמש - קרי ליה "אין צריך לאמו", כל חד לפום חורפיה. אלמא, מכי הוי בר חמש בעי לזכוייה, וטפי מבר ד' לא קרי ליה "צריך לאמו" דליפוק:
Rashi on Eruvin 82a:19:2.english: About four, about five - [The Gemara] calls him "one who does not need his mother," each one according to his precocity. Thus, once he is five [years old], one must confer possession [of the eiruv] upon him, and older than four, it does not call him "one who needs his mother" such that he may go out [by his mother's eiruv].

Rashi on Eruvin 82a:1:1.hebrew: גברא אגברא - דר' יהושע בן לוי אדשמואל. שמואל, דאמר הלכה, סבר פליגי, ור' יהושע סבר לא פליגי:
Rashi on Eruvin 82a:1:1.english: One person against another person - That of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi against that of Shmuel. Shmuel, who said "the halakha [is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda]," maintains [that] they disagree, and Rabbi Yehoshua maintains [that] they do not disagree.

Rashi on Eruvin 82a:3:1.hebrew: הפסולין - לעדות, דכולן גזלנין מדבריהן הן, דאסמכתא לא קנייא, ומגזל גזיל ליה:
Rashi on Eruvin 82a:3:1.english: The disqualified [ones] - For testimony, as all of them are robbers by rabbinic decree, for an asmakhta does not effect acquisition, and he is [effectively] robbing him.

Rashi on Eruvin 82a:3:3.english: Those who fly pigeons - [One who wagers:] “If your pigeon precedes mine [I will give you such-and-such].”

Rashi on Eruvin 82a:3:4.hebrew: סוחרי שביעית - דרחמנא אמר: ״לאכלה״ ולא לסחורה. וזה שחומד ממון לעבור עבירה על הממון — רשע הוא, והתורה אמרה: ״אל תשת רשע עד״ (שמות כג):
Rashi on Eruvin 82a:3:4.english: Merchants of the Sabbatical Year - For the Merciful One stated: "[It shall be] for eating" — and not for commerce; and this [person] who covets money [to the point of] committing a transgression for money is a wicked person, and the Torah said: "Do not set a wicked person as a witness" (Exodus 23).

Rashi on Eruvin 82a:4:1.hebrew: בזמן שאין להם אומנות אלא היא - דקסבר ר' יהודה: אסמכתא — שהוא נסמך על דעתו שהוא ינצחנו, ועל אותה אסמכתא הוא מתנה — קניא, ולאו גזלנין נינהו. ופסולייהו לפי שאין עסוקין בישובו של עולם; דכיון דאין מכירין ובקיאין בטורח וצער בני אדם, אינן חסין על חבריהן מלהפסידן ממון:
Rashi on Eruvin 82a:4:1.english: When they have no occupation other than this - For Rabbi Yehuda holds [that] an asmachta — [in] that he relies on his presumption that he will defeat him, and upon that reliance he stipulates — effects acquisition, and they are not robbers. And their disqualification is because they are not engaged in the settlement of the world; for since they do not recognize and are not familiar with the toil and pain of human beings, they do not spare their fellows from causing them monetary loss.

Rashi on Eruvin 82a:5:1.hebrew: וח"א כו' - קא ס"ד היינו ת"ק דמתניתין, אלמא אימתי לחלוק:
Rashi on Eruvin 82a:5:1.english: "And the Rabbis say," etc. - It enters the mind that this is the first tanna of the Mishnah, which implies that "when" is to dispute.

Rashi on Eruvin 82a:6:1.hebrew: ההיא - ברייתא משום ר"ט היא, דאמר אסמכתא לא קניא. אבל במתניתין לא פליג רבי יהודה אדתנא קמא, אלא מפרש לטעמיה:
Rashi on Eruvin 82a:6:1.english: That - [That] *baraita* is in the name of Rabbi Tarfon, who said [that] an *asmachta* does not effect acquisition. But in the Mishnah, Rabbi Yehuda does not disagree with the First Tanna, but rather explains his reasoning.

Rashi on Eruvin 82a:7:1.hebrew: אין אחד מהן נזיר - שנים שיושבין וראו אחד בא, ואמר אחד מהן: "הריני נזיר שזה נזיר", ואמר חבירו: "הריני נזיר שאין זה נזיר":
Rashi on Eruvin 82a:7:1.english: Neither one of them is a nazirite - [In the case of] two [people] who were sitting and saw someone coming, and one of them said: "I am hereby a nazirite [if] this [person] is a nazirite," and his fellow said: "I am hereby a nazirite [if] this [person] is not a nazirite."

Rashi on Eruvin 82a:7:2.hebrew: להפלאה - שיהא נדרו מפורש על הודאי, ולא בתורת ספק — אי נזיר אותו הבא כנגדו:
Rashi on Eruvin 82a:7:2.english: For clear pronunciation - That his vow must be clearly articulated concerning a certainty, and not in the manner of doubt — [such as] whether that one approaching him is a nazirite.

Rashi on Eruvin 82a:8:1.english: If he wins - If he wins.

Tosafot on Eruvin 82a:10:1.hebrew: כיצד משתתפין מניח את החבית - כל פירותיהם היו רגילים להניח בחבית, כדתניא לעיל [עירובין דף פ]: "מביאין אח החבית של יין, ושל שמן, ושל גרוגרות, ושל שאר כל מיני פירות":
Tosafot on Eruvin 82a:10:1.english: "How does one participate... he places the barrel" - They were accustomed to place all their produce in a barrel, as it is taught earlier [Eruvin daf 80]: "They bring the barrel of wine, and of oil, and of dried figs, and of all other types of produce."

Tosafot on Eruvin 82a:11:1.hebrew: אין מערבין אלא לדבר מצוה - לעול, דתנן: "אם באו נכרים למזרח וכו'" — ומוקי לה בגמ' בחרי מתא, ופי' שם בקונטרס שצריך לצעוק לפניו — הוי נמי דבר מצוה, שהולך לצורך בני עירו ומפקח על עסקי רבים:
Tosafot on Eruvin 82a:11:1.english: "One may establish an eiruv only for the purpose of a mitzvah" - Actually [le'olam], that which we learned [in a mishna]: "If gentiles came to the east, etc.," and [the Gemara] establishes it with regard to the town noble, and [Rashi] explained there in the Commentary that he needs to cry out before him — [this] is also a matter of a mitzvah, since he is going for the need of his townspeople and overseeing public affairs.

Tosafot on Eruvin 82a:13:1.hebrew: שמע מינה אין ברירה - דלא מסתבר דאחילו בעירובי תחומין דרבנן אין ברירה, כדאמרינן פרק בכל מערבין (לעיל עירובין דף לז:): מאן האי תנא דאפילו בדרבנן לית ליה ברירה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 82a:13:1.english: Learn from here [that] there is no retroactive clarification - For it is not reasonable that even regarding eiruvei techumin, which are rabbinic, there is no retroactive clarification, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Bekhol Me'arvin (above, Eruvin 37b): "Who is this tanna who does not accept retroactive clarification even regarding rabbinic [enactments]?"

Tosafot on Eruvin 82a:15:1.hebrew: קטן בן שש יוצא בעירוב אמו - אף על גב דאין מערבין אלא לדבר מצוה, מכל מקום יוצא קטן בעירוב אמו, דאי אפשר לה להניחו משום דכרוך אחריה. א"נ, בקטן נמי איכא מצוה לחנכו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 82a:15:1.english: A six-year-old child may go out by means of his mother’s eiruv - Even though one may establish an eiruv only for the sake of a mitzvah, nevertheless, a child may go out by means of his mother’s eiruv, as it is impossible for her to leave him [behind], since he is attached to her. Alternatively, with a child there is also a mitzvah: to educate him.

Tosafot on Eruvin 82a:3:1.english: "And these are those who are disqualified" - [This] is explained in the chapter [entitled] Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 24b).

Tosafot on Eruvin 82a:4:1.hebrew: אמר ר' יהודה אימתי כו' בזמן שאין לו אומנות כו' - אע"ג דמסקינן דפליגי רבנן עליה דרבי יהודה, הלכה כרבי יהודה, כדפסיק בפרק זה בורר (סנהדרין דף כו:): א"ר אבהו, הלכה כרבי יהודה. ומכאן משמע דשרי לשחוק בקוביא, דאפילו לרמי בר חמא, דמפרש טעמא דמשחק בקוביא פסול משום דאסמכתא לא קניא, היינו לרבנן; אבל לר' יהודה, דמכשר היכא דגמיר אומנות אחריתי, קסבר דכה"ג לאו אסמכתא היא. וטעם דלא הוי אסמכתא, כדפירש הקונטרס בפ' זה בורר (סנהדרין דף כד:), משום דלא דמי לההיא דב"ע (ד' קד:): "אם אוביר ולא איעביד אכלם אלפא זוזי", דהתם הוי בידו, ולהכי לא גמר ומקני, דמעיקרא כי אתני ארעתא דלא יהיב ליה אסמכתא קמתני, דטועה וסבור שלא יבא לידי כן; אבל הכא, לא סמיך אמידי, משום דלא ידע אי נצח או לא. ובפרק זה בורר (סנהדרין דף כה.) משמע גבי מפריחי יונים, דקאמר: "וצריכא, דאי תנא דתולה בדעת עצמו, התם הוא דאמר: קים לי בנפשאי דידענא ספי", ולהכי הוי אסמכתא; משמע היכא דבידו, הויא אסמכתא טפי. וקשה לר"ת, דבסוף איזהו נשך (ב"מ דף עג:) גבי האי דיהיב זוזי לחבריה למזבן ליה חמרא כו', ופריך: מ"ש דאם אוביר ולא איעביד אשלם במיטבא? ומשני: התם בידו, הכא לאו בידו; אלמא משום דלאו בידי הויא אסמכתא טפי! ונראה: היכא דבידו לגמרי ולא גזים, כי ההוא ד"אם אוביר ולא איעביד אשלם במיטבא", לא הויא אסמכתא; וכן היכא דאין בידו כלל ואפילו הכי גמיר ומקני, כגון קוביא וכה"ג. אבל היכא דבידו ולא בידו, כי ההוא חמרא דפשע ולא זבן ליה — ואע"ג דיין מצוי הרבה לקנות, מ"מ כיון דתלוי באחרים, דאם לא ירצו למכור לו, ממי יקנה? הלכך לא גמר ומקני, והוי אסמכתא גמורה. ועוד פר"ת טעם אחר: דדווקא כי ההוא ד"אם אני חוזר בי ערבוני מחול" דפרק הזהב (בבא מציעא דף מח:), ומי שפרע מקצת חובו והשליש את שטרו דגט פשוט (ב"ב דף קסח.), וכל כה"ג, חשיב אסמכתא, שאינו מתכוין אלא להסמיך חבירו על דבריו שיאמינוהו; אבל הכא, אדעתא דהכי קעבדו שירויחו או זה או זה. ואותם המשחקים באמנה, אומר ר"י דאינו חייב לשלם, דבמה יקנה? דלמ"ד אסמכתא היא, לא קני אפילו בקנין אלא בב"ד חשוב, כדמוכח בנדרים (דף כו:); ולמ"ד לאו אסמכתא היא, היאך יקנה בדברים בלא קנין בשביל שנוצח חבירו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 82a:4:1.english: "Rabbi Yehuda said: When [is this so]? When he has no occupation [other than this one]..." - Even though we conclude that the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Yehuda, the halakhah is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, as [the Gemara] rules in the chapter [entitled] Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 26b): Rabbi Abbahu said, the halakhah is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda. And from here it is implied that it is permitted to play with dice. For even according to Rami bar Ḥama, who explains that the reason a dice player is disqualified is that an asmakhta does not effect acquisition, that applies [only] according to the Rabbis; but according to Rabbi Yehuda, who qualifies [him] where he has mastered another occupation, he maintains that in such a case it is not an asmakhta. And the reason that it is not an asmakhta, as Rashi explained in the chapter [entitled] Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 24b), is because it is not similar to that [case] in Bava Metzia (104b): "If I leave [the field] uncultivated and do not work [it], I will pay one thousand zuz." For there, it was in his power [to work the field], and therefore he did not fully resolve to transfer ownership, since initially when he stipulated, [it was with the assumption] that he would not give [the money] to him — he made a conditional commitment because he erred and thought that it would not come to this. But here [in gambling], he relies on nothing, because he does not know whether he will win or not. And in the chapter [entitled] Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 25a), it is implied regarding pigeon racers, where [the Gemara] says: "And [both cases are] necessary, for if [the Mishnah] had taught [only the case where] he relies on his own skill — there it is because he says: I am certain of myself that I know how to feed [them properly]," and therefore it is an asmakhta; this implies that wherever it is in his power, it is more [likely to be] an asmakhta. And Rabbeinu Tam raised a difficulty: For at the end of [the chapter entitled] Eizehu Neshekh (Bava Metzia 73b), regarding that [person] who gave money to his fellow to buy wine for him, etc., and [the Gemara] asks: What is the difference from [the case of]: "If I leave [the field] uncultivated and do not work [it], I will pay from the best [produce]"? And [the Gemara] answers: There it is in his power, [whereas] here it is not in his power. Thus [we see] that because it is not in his power, it is more [likely to be] an asmakhta! And it appears: Where it is completely in his power and he did not exaggerate, like that [case] of: "If I leave [the field] uncultivated and do not work [it], I will pay from the best [produce]," it is not an asmakhta. And likewise, where it is not in his power at all, and even so he fully resolves to transfer ownership, such as dice and the like, [it is not an asmakhta]. But where it is [partially] in his power and [partially] not in his power, like that wine where he was negligent and did not buy it for him — and even though wine is commonly available to purchase, nevertheless, since it depends on others, for if they do not wish to sell to him, from whom will he buy? Therefore he did not fully resolve to transfer ownership, and it is a complete asmakhta. And furthermore, Rabbeinu Tam stated another reason: That specifically like that [case] of: "If I retract, my deposit shall be forfeit," in the chapter [entitled] Hazahav (Bava Metzia 48b), and one who paid part of his debt and deposited his promissory note with a third party, in [the chapter entitled] Get Pashut (Bava Batra 168a), and anything of this sort, is considered an asmakhta, because his intention is only to have his fellow rely on his words so that he will believe him; but here, they act with the intention that either this one or that one will win [and profit]. And regarding those who gamble on credit, Ri says that he is not obligated to pay. For through what would [the winner] acquire [the money]? For according to the one who says it is an asmakhta, he does not acquire even with a formal act of acquisition (kinyan), unless [it was performed] in an esteemed court, as is proved in Nedarim (26b); and according to the one who says it is not an asmakhta, how could he acquire through mere words, without a kinyan, just because his fellow was defeated [in the game]?
